pathophysiology.summary: AF is a supraventricular arrhythmia with disorganised atrial activity and an irregular ventricular response. Loss of atrial contraction causes stasis in the left atrial appendage, so thrombus and stroke are the main risks; fast ventricular rates cause symptoms and can impair left ventricular function.
keyMechanisms: Triggers (often pulmonary vein ectopy) act on a remodelled atrium (hypertension, valve disease, ageing, obesity).
Atrial stasis → left atrial appendage thrombus → embolic stroke.

symptoms: Palpitations, breathlessness, dizziness or syncope, chest discomfort; may be asymptomatic (NICE 1.1.1).
Stroke or TIA may be the first presentation.
physicalSigns: Irregularly irregular pulse; pulse deficit; signs of heart failure or valve disease.
redFlags: Haemodynamic instability (shock, ischaemia, acute heart failure) — emergency electrical cardioversion (NICE 1.8.1)
Acute decompensated heart failure — senior input; avoid calcium-channel blockers (NICE 1.8.3)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Regular sawtooth flutter waves; same stroke risk assessment (NICE 1.2.1).
Discrete P waves of varying shape.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Irregular RR intervals without P waves.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Confirms diagnosis; ambulatory ECG if paroxysmal (NICE 1.1.3).

references.title: NICE NG196: Atrial fibrillation: diagnosis and management

clinicalManagement.title: Acute presentation
actions: Life-threatening instability: emergency electrical cardioversion without waiting for anticoagulation (NICE 1.8.1).
Stable, onset under 48 hours: rate or rhythm control; over 48 hours or uncertain: rate control (NICE 1.8.2).
Pharmacological cardioversion: flecainide or amiodarone if no structural heart disease; amiodarone if structural disease (NICE 1.8.5).
Start heparin at presentation if not anticoagulated (NICE 1.8.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Stroke prevention
actions: Saudi MOH: oral anticoagulation for intermediate or high stroke risk; suggests NOAC rather than VKA (dabigatran 150 mg twice daily, rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily or apixaban 5 mg twice daily).
NICE: DOAC if CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more; consider for men with 1; none if 0 (men) or 1 (women) under 65.
Do not use aspirin alone for stroke prevention (NICE 1.6.14); do not withhold for age or falls (NICE 1.6.8).
Warfarin if DOACs are unsuitable (including mechanical valves); aim TTR 65% or more (NICE 1.6.11).

clinicalManagement.title: Rate control (first line for most)
actions: Beta-blocker (not sotalol) or diltiazem/verapamil (NICE 1.7.2); in heart failure follow heart-failure guidance (NICE 1.7.3).
Digoxin monotherapy if sedentary or other options unsuitable (NICE 1.7.4); combination if needed (1.7.5).
No amiodarone for long-term rate control (NICE 1.7.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Rhythm control
actions: Consider if symptoms persist despite rate control, reversible cause, AF-caused heart failure or new onset (NICE 1.7.1, 1.7.7).
AF over 48 hours: anticoagulate at least 3 weeks before cardioversion (NICE 1.8.6).
No flecainide/propafenone in ischaemic or structural heart disease (NICE 1.7.9); amiodarone in LV impairment (NICE 1.7.13).
Catheter ablation if drugs fail or are unsuitable (NICE 1.7.19).

adjustments: 2.5 mg twice daily if 2 of: age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more (label)
Not studied below CrCl 30 (Saudi MOH remarks)
monitoring: Renal function, Hb, bleeding at least annually

lifestyleAndDiet: Reduce alcohol; weight loss; treat sleep apnoea and hypertension.

dischargeCriteria: Stable rate, anticoagulation started with counselling, follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review anticoagulation need, bleeding risk and renal function at least annually (NICE 1.6.16–1.6.17); review stroke risk at 65 or new comorbidity if not anticoagulated (NICE 1.6.15).
